audit.name: Controlled-fire pyrotechnology
audit.ageGap: root (no prerequisites)
audit.effectRationale: Managed hearths and earth ovens make tough roots, seeds and bone grease edible: a wider fallback diet lets a band absorb lean seasons.
audit.costConcern: 1,050 is double the other A1 roots (knapping 520) but justified: seven dependents across energy, materials, transport and communication.
audit.rationale: Root of the pyrotechnology family with seven dependents; no prerequisite is needed (fire itself is baseline, D-047 ruling 2). Effect is food security from earth-oven processing, kept distinct from the lamp's underground-light role.

audit.name: Oil lamp

prereqAssessment.why: A fat lamp is a controlled, sustained small flame; it presupposes deliberate fire management.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Portable light makes underground work possible: ochre and flint mining (Lion Cave ~40 kya; chalk-cut lamps in Neolithic flint mines) depend on it.
audit.costConcern: 180 is the cheapest node in the lane; appropriate for a one-step extension of fire.
audit.rationale: Keep its own prerequisite. It is a leaf today, but underground mining needs light: propose that mining_shaft (T2, A3) gains lamp as a prerequisite (chalk-cut lamps at Grimes Graves, Spiennes-type flint shafts). Routed to the integrator, not applied from this record.

audit.name: Charcoal making

prereqAssessment.why: Tar making is pyrolysis of wood in a sealed, oxygen-starved pit: the same principle as a covered charcoal pile.
Felling and splitting the cordwood for a clamp needs ground-edge axes.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Charcoal carries about twice the heat of firewood per load, so a settlement can draw its fuel from further out: pre-industrial cities ringed themselves with charcoal-burning zones beyond the firewood belt.
audit.costConcern: 1,050 for an A2 node is in line with the A2 cohort.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are sound. Its only dependent is iron_bloomery; T2 has already proposed copper_smelting += charcoal, which closes the obvious missing edge (smelting needs a reducing fuel).

audit.name: Bellows

prereqAssessment.why: Pot and bag bellows are leather diaphragms or bags; hide working supplies the material.
Controlled draught through a fired chamber is the furnace concept the bellows intensifies.

audit.ageGap: hide_working A1 (3 Ages earlier: long-standing enabler, kept); kiln_updraft A2 (2 Ages earlier: long-standing enabler, kept)
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane: industry, materials
audit.effectRationale: A forced-draught forge lets the village smith re-draw, re-temper and mend edges; tools in use wear out more slowly.
audit.costConcern: 2,960 sits at the A4 level; at A3 it would be on the high side of the A3 cohort, which the per-(tree, Age) scale absorbs.
audit.rationale: Its own emerged date (~1,500 BCE, Rekhmire tomb) lies inside the A3 window (~3,500-1,200 BCE), so the A4 label contradicts the dating. Moving it fills the empty A3 energy cohort. Prerequisites (A1, A2) and dependents (cast_iron A5, blast_furnace_water A6) stay order-safe.

audit.name: Water mill

prereqAssessment.why: The mill drives a rotary millstone pair; the quern gives the stone geometry and the rynd/spindle.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Hand-grinding grain consumed hours of household labour daily; a mill releases that labour to the fields. Landmark node (first non-muscle prime mover), hence a larger delta.
audit.costConcern: 11,830 is very high for A5 (trip_hammer 1,760); justified as the gateway of eight dependents, but the integrator's A5 scale should check it does not dominate the A5 cohort.
audit.rationale: Prerequisite kept. gearing (~150 BCE) is not added: the earliest mills (Perachora ~300 BCE horizontal mill) need no right-angle gearing and the node predates gearing. Live unlocks retained.

audit.name: Water-powered trip hammer

prereqAssessment.why: A cam on a water-wheel shaft lifting a hammer: needs the water-power wheel.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Water-driven stamps crush ore at the mine and hull grain, multiplying what each extractor delivers.
audit.costConcern: 1,760 is low against water_mill (11,830); acceptable for an extension node.
audit.rationale: Prerequisite correct; China first (Han ~40 BCE). Effect differs from water_mill (extraction vs farm labour).

audit.name: Vertical-axis windmill

prereqAssessment.why: The panemone drives the same millstone arrangement as the horizontal water mill.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Sistan windmills ground grain and lifted water for gardens (al-Mas'udi, al-Istakhri): wind-lifted irrigation raises yields in arid land.
audit.rationale: Prerequisite correct. Deliberate leaf: the Persian type is a regional branch independent of the European post mill. Live unlock shared with windmill_post, so a distinct operand effect distinguishes the two.

audit.name: Post mill

prereqAssessment.why: Millstone, spindle and miller's craft come from the water mill.
Sail cloth and rigging on the sweeps; the mill's sails are a land use of sailmaking.
PROPOSED ADDITION: a horizontal-axis rotor must turn a vertical stone spindle through a right-angle gear (brake wheel and wallower); gear trains (~150 BCE) are the real enabling knowledge.

audit.ageGap: sail_square A3 (3 Ages earlier: long-standing enabler, kept)
audit.effectRationale: Milling without a river head spreads mechanical grinding to flat, riverless farmland, releasing household labour where water mills cannot be built.
audit.costConcern: 4,970 is over twice windmill_vertical; acceptable given its three prerequisites.
audit.rationale: Add gearing: the post mill is defined by its right-angle drive, and water_mill does not imply gearing in this graph (its anchor is the gearless horizontal mill). gearing is A5 (~150 BCE), well before 1,180 CE.

audit.name: Atmospheric steam engine

prereqAssessment.why: Newcomen's engine works by atmospheric pressure against a condensed-steam vacuum (Torricelli, Guericke, Papin).
Large cylinders and pipework; Coalbrookdale cast Newcomen cylinders from 1718.

audit.ageGap: cast_iron A5 (2 Ages earlier: long-standing enabler, kept)
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane: materials, science
audit.effectRationale: Mine drainage: engines kept coal and tin mines working below the water table, a step change in extraction. Larger delta as the first heat engine.
audit.costConcern: 23,650 is the most expensive A7 energy node; fine as the sole A7 energy node and a landmark.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites sound and minimal. Its date (1712) fits A7. coal_fuel (new) is not made a prerequisite: the invention needed vacuum physics and casting, not coal.

audit.name: Separate condenser

prereqAssessment.why: Watt improved a Newcomen model engine; the condenser is a modification of that engine.
Redundant through steam_atmospheric, but harmless; it documents the vacuum principle the condenser exploits.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Quartered fuel use made pumping engines economic at metal mines away from coalfields (Cornish tin and copper).
audit.costConcern: 5,910 is cheap against its parent (23,650) and steam_rotary (133,810): a 22x jump between consecutive steam nodes is a pacing outlier the A8 scale should smooth.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites kept (one is redundant but explanatory). Effect continues the mining role at a smaller delta than the first engine.

audit.name: Rotary steam engine

prereqAssessment.why: Rotary Watt engines were condensing engines.
Wilkinson's 1774 boring mill made Watt's cylinders tight enough to work.
Converting reciprocation to rotation (crank, or sun-and-planet gear to evade the crank patent).

audit.ageGap: crank_connecting_rod A6 (2 Ages earlier: long-standing enabler, kept)
audit.effectRationale: Factory power anywhere: mills leave the rivers and a much larger share of the population can work as non-farm specialists. Landmark node.
audit.costConcern: 133,810 is the largest A8 energy cost; it is the gateway to eight dependents, so a high cost is defensible, but see the condenser note.
audit.rationale: All three atoms are historically necessary. It is the Age VIII milestone fact (ages.json a8_steam).

audit.name: High-pressure steam

prereqAssessment.why: Trevithick's engines were double-acting rotary engines run at higher pressure.
Wrought-iron boiler plate strong enough for high pressure.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Compact high-pressure engines became portable engines: steam threshing and farm power (1840s-50s) raised output per farm worker. Transport uses belong to locomotive and steamboat.
audit.costConcern: 5,910 is light for its significance; acceptable as an extension.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites sound. Effect chosen so it does not double-count the transport nodes it gates.

audit.name: Dynamo

prereqAssessment.why: Faraday's induction is the principle of the generator.
A generator needs a rotary prime mover.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Current on demand for laboratories: electrochemistry, electroplating and physics experiments no longer depend on batteries.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites correct and minimal. Effect is modest; the dynamo's large consequences arrive through electricity_generation.

audit.name: Incandescent lamp

prereqAssessment.why: The incandescent bulb depends on a high vacuum (Sprengel pump, 1865), descended from the air pump.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Enclosed electric light replaces candles, oil and gas flames indoors; fewer house fires, so dwellings last longer.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites sound. Effect differs from every other A8 energy node.

audit.name: Central power station and grid

prereqAssessment.why: Lighting was the demand that justified Pearl Street and Holborn Viaduct (1882).

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Genuine live unlocks (power station, grid); no operand effect is added so the electricity capacity system carries the effect.
audit.costConcern: 47,310 fine for the Age IX milestone node.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites kept. Relies on its live unlocks, which is permitted for a genuine entity unlock.

audit.name: Electric motor

prereqAssessment.why: Motors are useful once supply is distributed.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Electric lifts (Siemens 1880, Otis electric 1889) and pumps make tall apartment blocks liveable: more people per dwelling footprint.
audit.rationale: Prerequisite correct (electromagnetism implied). Effect distinct within A8 energy.

audit.name: High-speed petrol engine

prereqAssessment.why: Daimler and Maybach worked at Deutz on the Otto engine; the petrol engine is its fast, light derivative.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: The node includes the first motor vehicles (Benz 1886): powered road travel is faster than horse travel.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites sound. automobile_mass (transport) extends the road effect at scale.

audit.name: Turbojet

prereqAssessment.why: Jet engines fly in metal monoplanes.
Axial and centrifugal turbine aerodynamics came from steam turbines (Parsons; Brown Boveri).

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Jet aviation shrinks long-distance travel time: migrants can move further for the same cost.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites sound. superalloy (~1940) is not added because it post-dates the node's 1939 date.

audit.name: Steam turbine

prereqAssessment.why: Steel discs and blades for high rotational speed.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane: materials, science
audit.effectRationale: Turbine steamers (Turbinia 1897, Mauretania 1907) cut ocean passage times so price differences between ports close faster; unit.aircraft_carrier is not a live unlock.
audit.costConcern: 66,900 heavy for A8; the integrator's A8 scale absorbs it.
audit.rationale: Dated 1884 (Parsons), well inside A8 (1750-1914); all prerequisites are A8 and its impact (turbo-alternators, turbine liners, Dreadnought) is pre-1914. Dependents jet_engine and nuclear_power stay A9, so the move is order-safe.

audit.name: Diesel engine

prereqAssessment.why: Steel strong enough for compression-ignition pressures.
Diesel set out to realise a Carnot-efficient cycle.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane: materials, science
audit.effectRationale: Diesel ships (Selandia 1912), lorries and locomotives haul bulk cargo at much lower fuel cost.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites sound. Dated 1897 (A8 window) but kept A9: its economic effect (motor ships, lorries, diesel rail) comes after 1912; flagged in findings as an A8/A9 boundary case.

audit.name: Stored-program computer

prereqAssessment.why: The stored-program machine succeeded plugboard machines (ENIAC to EDVAC report).
Stored-program memory came from radar: Williams-Kilburn CRT store (Manchester) and mercury delay lines (EDSAC).

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Administrative computing: LEO payroll (1951), UNIVAC for the US Census (1951), later tax processing; administrative reach extends further.
audit.costConcern: 267,620 is the A9 maximum; acceptable for the gateway of fourteen dependents.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites correct; the radar edge is historically exact (memory technology). Age IX milestone fact.

audit.name: Transistor

prereqAssessment.why: Amplifier and switching circuitry of tube electronics; Bell Labs set out to replace the tube.
Band theory and doping are the physical basis.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Cheap battery transistor radios (from 1954) carried news, music and political speech into villages: more civic and cultural engagement per person.
audit.costConcern: 133,810 high; check against the A9 scale.

audit.name: Integrated circuit

prereqAssessment.why: ICs are many transistors on one die.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Genuine live unlock (semiconductor fab); no operand effect added.
audit.costConcern: 267,620 at the A9 maximum; heavy for a node with one live unlock.

audit.name: Microprocessor
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Microprocessor point-of-sale terminals and barcode scanning (UPC, 1974) give live stock control: goods move from store to shelf faster.

audit.name: Nuclear power-plant engineering
audit.prereq: (graphite_reactor OR heavy_water_reactor OR light_water_reactor OR fast_breeder_reactor) AND steam_turbine AND electricity_generation

prereqAssessment.why: One of four reactor families (Obninsk, Calder Hall).

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Genuine live unlock (nuclear power station).
audit.rationale: The OR over reactor families is the right shape (any one family suffices). Deliberate leaf: the station is the terminal capability.

audit.name: Hydroelectric dam

prereqAssessment.why: Niagara power reached Buffalo by AC lines.
Francis and Pelton turbines drive the generators.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Multi-purpose dams (Hoover 1936, Aswan) store floods and release water through dry years: steadier irrigated harvests.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites sound. Dated 1895 (A8 window) but kept A9: the large multi-purpose dams that carry its effect are 1930s onwards; noted as a boundary case.

audit.name: Photovoltaic cell

prereqAssessment.why: The 1954 silicon cell came out of Bell Labs' transistor doping work.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane: engineering, science
audit.effectRationale: Genuine live unlock (solar farm).

audit.name: Lithium-ion battery

prereqAssessment.why: Solid-state chemistry of the cathode materials.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Light rechargeable power for field radios, night-vision, sensors and small drones extends what a formation can see.

audit.name: Very-large-scale integration
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Cheap abundant computation underpins the electronics and software industries: a larger specialist workforce becomes possible.

audit.name: Combined-cycle gas turbine
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Gas-fired combined cycle displaced coal plant; far less particulate and sulphur pollution means fewer deaths from dirty air.

audit.name: Modern wind turbine
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Genuine live unlock (wind farm).
audit.rationale: Prerequisites sound; deliberate leaf (terminal generation capability).

audit.name: Grid-scale energy storage
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Buffered supply keeps refrigerated stores and cold chains running through outages: less food spoils in store.
audit.rationale: The OR correctly admits both historical routes. Deliberate leaf.

audit.name: Smart grid
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Real-time pricing and demand response let supply and demand meet across regions within minutes: price gaps close faster.

audit.name: High-level programming languages
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: FORTRAN (formula translation, 1957) let scientists program their own calculations: universities do research more cheaply.

audit.name: Operating system

prereqAssessment.why: Systems software is written in higher-level languages (Multics PL/I, Unix C).

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Time-sharing (CTSS, Dartmouth DTSS 1964) put a whole campus on one machine: new universities reach full capability sooner.

audit.name: Relational database
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Transaction systems at national scale: tax records, withholding and VAT matching let a state collect what it assesses.

audit.name: Personal computer
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Office and computer skills became the ladder into clerical and technical classes: faster social promotion.

audit.name: Public-key cryptography
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Secure payment and contracts over open networks (SSL, 1995) let buyers and sellers anywhere trade: prices converge faster.

audit.name: Parallel processors
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: General-purpose GPU computing (CUDA 2007) accelerates simulation in physics, chemistry, genomics and climate: more research per researcher.

audit.name: Machine learning
audit.ageGap: probability_statistics A7 (2 Ages earlier: long-standing enabler, kept)
audit.effectRationale: Computer-aided diagnosis: neural-network mammography screening (ImageChecker, FDA 1998) lets university medicine catch disease earlier.

audit.name: Deep learning
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Neural machine translation and speech recognition lower the language barrier for people who move.

audit.name: Large language models

prereqAssessment.why: Training corpora come from the web.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Knowledge assistance for researchers and for learners: tutoring and coding help speed both research and the acquisition of specialist skills.

audit.name: Cloud computing
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Genuine live unlock (data centre).

audit.name: Smartphone
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane: communication, energy
audit.effectRationale: Mobile price information collapses price dispersion (Kerala fish markets, Jensen 2007), and maps and messaging let migrants travel further.

audit.name: Cyber operations

prereqAssessment.why: Attacking and defending encrypted, authenticated systems.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Network intrusion is intelligence collection: reading an adversary's systems reveals the dispositions of its formations.

audit.name: Quantum computing (early)
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Noisy quantum processors serve mainly as research instruments for quantum simulation: a small research gain.

audit.name: Numerical weather prediction

prereqAssessment.why: ENIAC ran the first numerical forecast (1950).
Radiosondes and telegraphed observations feed the model.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Farmers time sowing, spraying and harvest by forecast and get warning of frosts and storms: harvests vary less.

audit.name: Fusion power

prereqAssessment.why: Commercial fusion follows the research programme.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Genuine live unlock (fusion plant).
audit.rationale: Prerequisite correct (superconducting magnets presumably inside nuclear_fusion_research).

audit.name: Fault-tolerant quantum computing

prereqAssessment.why: Error correction scales the early machines.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: The flagship application is simulating catalysts such as nitrogenase (FeMoco) for cheaper nitrogen fertiliser: higher yields per km2.

audit.name: General machine intelligence

prereqAssessment.why: The current route to broad machine capability.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Automation of cognitive work: far more specialist output per person and administration that reaches everywhere.

audit.name: Space-based solar power
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: Firm power without fuel imports removes fuel-price shocks, a recurrent trigger of unrest (fuel riots, 1970s oil shocks). project.probe_acceleration is not a live unlock.

audit.name: Energy conversion

prereqAssessment.why: Either modern generation route opens the repeatable.
Either modern generation route opens the repeatable.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: REPEATABLE: each level should advance farming.yieldPerArableKm2PerYear (suggested gapFraction 0.06): cheaper energy cuts the cost of nitrogen fertiliser (Haber-Bosch) and irrigation pumping, the main energy-to-food channel.
audit.rationale: OR is right (either modern route). Becomes a repeatable level node; one operand only.

audit.name: Computation
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: REPEATABLE: each level should advance governance.authorityDecayCostUnits (suggested gapFraction 0.06), matching its text (administration and automation efficiency); the operand's cap 3.0 leaves room.

audit.name: Cyber research
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: REPEATABLE: each level should advance fog.formationSightNodes (offence: intelligence, gapFraction 0.05) and society.unrestOutputDrag (defence: hardened infrastructure keeps output flowing through disruption, gapFraction 0.05). The text calls it relative; no relative operand exists, so absolute operands stand in.

audit.name: AC power transmission

prereqAssessment.why: Transmission carries station output (induction knowledge implied).

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: 'Coal by wire': power generated at the mine mouth or the falls reaches cities by line instead of coal by rail and barge, reducing bulk haulage.

audit.name: Stationary gas engine

prereqAssessment.why: Engine design lineage (Lenoir adapted a double-acting steam engine layout).
PROPOSED: replace with town_gas (new). Lenoir and Otto engines ran on piped coal gas; town_gas carries the gas chemistry (it requires chemistry_quantitative itself), so the edge becomes specific.
Precision machined cylinders and valve gear.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane: industry, science
audit.effectRationale: Boiler-less engines small and cheap enough for a master craftsman's workshop let small trades mechanise: more artisans rise to skilled-master status.
audit.costConcern: 56,260 high against internal_combustion (47,310), its own successor; flag for the A8 scale.
audit.rationale: The engine's fuel was town gas; without a gas-supply node the bridge is missing. The replacement keeps chemistry_quantitative transitively.

audit.name: Water turbine

prereqAssessment.why: Euler's turbine equation; Fourneyron's design is engineered from theory.

audit.ageGap: water_mill A5 (3 Ages earlier: long-standing enabler, kept)
audit.effectRationale: Turbine-driven sawmills (Lowell-era New England) cut boards with thin kerfs instead of hewing: less timber per dwelling (balloon frame era).

audit.name: Fast breeder reactors

prereqAssessment.why: A breeder fuel cycle needs plutonium separated from spent fuel (nuclear_fission implied).

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: A closed fuel cycle makes generation independent of uranium and oil imports: embargoes and strikes cost less output.

audit.name: Geological waste disposal
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane: medicine, science
audit.effectRationale: Isolating long-lived waste from groundwater avoids chronic exposure (small mortality gain), and a credible repository defuses the local siting disputes that waste storage provokes (small grievance relief).
audit.costConcern: 94,620 high for a leaf with a minimal effect; candidate for a lower magnitude.

audit.name: Graphite-moderated reactors

prereqAssessment.why: Aluminium-canned fuel slugs at X-10 and Hanford.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane: materials, science
audit.effectRationale: Production piles supplied radioisotope tracers to laboratories (Oak Ridge isotope distribution from 1946): cheaper research in biology and chemistry.

audit.name: Heavy-water reactors

prereqAssessment.why: Pressurised coolant circuits of power variants.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: NRX at Chalk River made the cobalt-60 for the first teletherapy units (1951): university hospitals treat cancer more effectively.

audit.name: Light-water reactors
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.effectRationale: The standard civil reactor made large blocks of cheap baseload power available to industry: a larger specialist workforce is sustainable.
audit.costConcern: 189,240 very high relative to the other reactor families; flag.

audit.name: Programmable digital computer

prereqAssessment.why: The numerical analysis the machines were built for (ballistic tables).

audit.ageGap: calculus A7 (2 Ages earlier: long-standing enabler, kept)
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane: communication, science
audit.effectRationale: Colossus broke Lorenz traffic and revealed German dispositions before D-Day; ENIAC and Z3 automated scientific calculation.
audit.rationale: The OR is right (independent valve and relay routes).

audit.name: Spent-fuel reprocessing

prereqAssessment.why: Remote handling and shielding of hot cells.

audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane: medicine, science
audit.effectRationale: PUREX solvent extraction became general hydrometallurgy (copper SX-EW from 1968, rare-earth separation): more metal from each tonne of ore.

audit.name: Uranium enrichment
audit.ageGap: all prerequisites from the same or the previous Age
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane: materials, science
audit.effectRationale: The enrichment complexes (Oak Ridge, Sverdlovsk-44) trained tens of thousands of technicians, a lasting pipeline into skilled classes.

newNodes.name: Lifting crane
newNodes.emerged: ~515 BCE Greece (lewis and tong holes in temple blocks; pulley cranes); ~1st c. BCE Rome (treadwheel crane, polyspastos)
newNodes.prereqRationale: cordage: hoisting ropes. wheel_solid: the axle-and-drum winch (windlass) is the crane's drive. ashlar_masonry: dressed blocks with lewis holes are what cranes were built to lift. All dated millennia before the node.
newNodes.desc: A timber jib with pulleys and a winch lifts heavy blocks and beams: small gangs raise walls and roofs that once needed ramps and crowds.
newNodes.effectRationale: Cranes replace earthen ramps and large hauling crews: buildings take less labour.
newNodes.distinctFrom: mechanics_archimedean (A5) is the theory of the lever and compound pulley; the crane is the practical builder's machine, about 250 years earlier.
newNodes.rationale: cordage: hoisting ropes. wheel_solid: the axle-and-drum winch (windlass) is the crane's drive. ashlar_masonry: dressed blocks with lewis holes are what cranes were built to lift. All dated millennia before the node.

newNodes.name: Coal as fuel
newNodes.emerged: ~1,000 CE Northern Song China (coal for iron smelting and heating at Kaifeng); ~1,250 CE London sea-coal from Newcastle
newNodes.prereqRationale: mining_shaft: coal is won from pits and bell-pit shafts. bellows: coal burns well only under forced draught in forges and furnaces. Both dated far earlier.
newNodes.desc: Mining and burning mineral coal for heating, lime-burning, forging and smelting, where firewood has grown scarce.
newNodes.effectRationale: Shipped coal frees a city from its firewood belt (London and Newcastle sea-coal), and a coal miner wins far more heat per year than a woodcutter.
newNodes.distinctFrom: coke (A7) is coal carbonised for blast furnaces; this node is the earlier use of raw coal as a fuel. charcoal (A2) is a wood fuel.
newNodes.rationale: mining_shaft: coal is won from pits and bell-pit shafts. bellows: coal burns well only under forced draught in forges and furnaces. Both dated far earlier.

newNodes.name: Mine pumping engines
newNodes.emerged: ~1,556 CE Agricola, De re metallica (water-wheel and horse-gin rag-and-chain and rod pumps, Central European mines)
newNodes.prereqRationale: water_mill: the water wheel drives the pumps. crank_connecting_rod: turns rotation into the reciprocating stroke of rod pumps. mining_shaft: the shafts being drained. All dated earlier.
newNodes.desc: Water wheels and horse gins drive chains of pumps and lifting rods that keep deep mine shafts dry.
newNodes.effectRationale: Drained shafts reach ore below the water table: each extractor works richer, deeper ground.
newNodes.distinctFrom: steam_atmospheric (A7, 1712) drains mines with a heat engine; this node is the water- and animal-powered pumping it replaced.
newNodes.rationale: water_mill: the water wheel drives the pumps. crank_connecting_rod: turns rotation into the reciprocating stroke of rod pumps. mining_shaft: the shafts being drained. All dated earlier.

newNodes.name: Coal-gas lighting
newNodes.emerged: 1792 CE Murdoch lights his house at Redruth with coal gas; 1812 CE Gas Light and Coke Company, London
newNodes.prereqRationale: coke: gas is made by carbonising coal in closed retorts, the coke-making process. chemistry_quantitative (1789): gas purification and the chemistry of combustible gases. Both dated before 1792.
newNodes.desc: Coal is baked in retorts and the gas piped under the streets to burners: lit streets, mills, homes, and later fuel for gas engines.
newNodes.effectRationale: Gas-lit streets, reading rooms, mechanics' institutes and theatres moved civic and cultural life into the evening.
newNodes.distinctFrom: electric_light (A8, 1879) is electric incandescence; this is the earlier piped coal-gas supply, also the fuel of gas_engine.
newNodes.rationale: coke: gas is made by carbonising coal in closed retorts, the coke-making process. chemistry_quantitative (1789): gas purification and the chemistry of combustible gases. Both dated before 1792.

findings: Dependency and Age changes proposed: 4 applied through newPrereq/newAge (windmill_post += gearing; gas_engine chemistry_quantitative -> town_gas; bellows A4 -> A3 by its own ~1,500 BCE date; steam_turbine A9 -> A8 by its 1884 date). Two cross-group edges are routed to the integrator, not applied here: mining_shaft (T2) += lamp (underground light), coke (T2) += coal_fuel (coke presupposes coal use).

Engineering lane was A9-only (24 computing nodes) and energy had empty A3 and single-node A4/A7 cohorts. Fill: bellows moves into A3; new lifting_crane (A4) and mine_pumping_engines (A7) give engineering a pre-modern mechanical strand; coal_fuel (A6) and town_gas (A8) close the fuel chain (charcoal -> coal -> coke -> town gas -> gas engine).

A8/A9 boundary is inconsistent for 1880-1900 nodes: electricity_generation (1882), ac_transmission, electric_motor, internal_combustion are A8 while steam_turbine (1884), hydroelectric (1895), diesel (1897) are A9. Only steam_turbine is moved (its effect is pre-1914); hydroelectric and diesel are kept A9 because their effect comes after 1914.

Pacing outliers for the per-(tree, Age) scale: steam_separate_condenser 5,910 sits between 23,650 and 133,810; water_mill 11,830 is 7x trip_hammer at A5; gas_engine 56,260 exceeds its successor internal_combustion; light_water_reactor and uranium_enrichment 189,240 and computer/integrated_circuit/programmable_computer 267,620 are the A9 maxima; geological_disposal 94,620 is heavy for a leaf.

Live unlocks carry 11 nodes (water_mill, both windmills, electricity_generation, nuclear_power, hydroelectric, solar_pv, wind_turbine_modern, fusion_power, integrated_circuit, cloud_computing); 7 rely on the unlock alone. steam_turbine (unit.aircraft_carrier) and space_solar (project.probe_acceleration) have non-live unlocks and get operand effects.

Cap watch: research.researchPointsCoefficient from this group is 0.05 (gpu_parallel, large_language_models, quantum_computing) against a 0.3 cap shared with science and T2 (0.15); institutions.universities.maxResearchCostReduction reaches 0.11 of its 0.5 cap from this group alone. production.outputPerExtractorPerYear reaches 0.22 (cap 3.0); mobility.targetShareCap 0.18 (cap 1.0).

frontier_* repeatables: frontier_energy -> farming.yieldPerArableKm2PerYear (energy to fertiliser and pumping), frontier_computation -> governance.authorityDecayCostUnits, frontier_cyber -> fog.formationSightNodes + society.unrestOutputDrag. frontier_cyber is described as RELATIVE; the registry has no relative operand, so the engine track should decide whether absolute operands are acceptable.

The nuclear sub-family (graphite, heavy-water, light-water, breeder, reprocessing, enrichment, disposal) is knowledge-only by design; each now has a distinct, small spill-over effect (isotopes, Co-60 therapy, solvent extraction, fuel independence) rather than a duplicated power effect, since nuclear_power carries the station unlock.
